description:
Hello! We are SkyMetal, a sextet driven by curiosity, innovation, and a fascination with the universe and its endless possibilities.

We are students from different backgrounds and fields of knowledge who share a common purpose: to learn, explore new ideas, and build knowledge collaboratively. We believe in the transformative power of education, science, and technology as ways to connect people, break boundaries, and make knowledge increasingly accessible, diverse, and global.

More than just a team, we are individuals united by the desire to discover, create, and explore the unknown. After all, great discoveries begin with the curiosity to go beyond!
summary: Taking on the challenge of simplifying NASA data and translating it into a playable, educational alternative for children aged 7 to 12, simulating a realistic mission, SkyMetal developed the game Under Space. The game presents data provided by NASA in a playful way to depict the journey of the player, who has been recruited to take part in a lunar mission, designed to simulate a future mission to Mars. Your mission is to keep the lunar base operational for 14 days by managing available resources, protecting the crew from radiation, and gathering data for Mars, all while navigating conflicting demands. Challenges include collecting energy, water, and oxygen resources through minigames and balancing the interplay between tasks and resource consumption, requiring careful management so your actions don't cause the mission to fail! Featuring a cozy, nostalgic interface, this RPG guides the player through quests based on real problems and scenarios, powered by data from actual NASA instruments such as DONKI, OSDR, MoonTrek, and RadLab, turning science into action.
details:
WHAT IT DOES OR HOW IT WORKS?

The game unfolds through completing missions and tasks that arise over the days to manage the lunar base, while gradually collecting data to support a future mission to Mars. Before starting, the child selects their preferred character, country, and gender, and enters their name. From there, the story of “Under Space” begins with the character being recruited to participate in an ARTEMIS program mission, serving as a simulation to develop future missions to Mars. They will have to keep the lunar base operational for a month by managing resources, performing maintenance, protecting the crew from radiation, collecting rocks, sending daily reports and achievements back to Earth, and, above all, trying to survive unexpected events.

WHAT ARE THE BENEFITS?

→ The game simplifies NASA data in a playful and educational way so that children aged 7 to 12 can experience a NASA mission right from home. By focusing on younger generations, the game makes resource management and learning more engaging, sparking greater interest in astronomy and making NASA data accessible to a wide variety of audiences.

WHAT IS THE PROJECT'S INTENDED IMPACT? 

→ As the journey progresses, the player learns to gather and manage resources, understand simplified data collected and released by NASA, and learn about space missions and how projects such as ARTEMIS, PRIME-1, LCROSS, and MoonTrek operate through the activities and challenges they face. Players are also given the option to access references and find more related information, allowing them to deepen their knowledge using verified data. Ultimately, the primary goal is to share NASA data in an accessible way, illustrate the demands of living as an astronaut in harsh environments while juggling conflicting priorities, and inspire younger generations to take an interest in space exploration. 

WEB LANGUAGES AND TECHNOLOGIES 

  • HTML5: Game structure, delivered as a single file that runs directly in the browser with no installation required.
  • CSS3: Layout and responsiveness using container query units (cqw), animations, and the visual theme for panels and dialogues.
  • Vanilla JavaScript (no frameworks): All game logic, including the day cycle, resources, missions, events, decisions, and consequences.
  • Canvas 2D API: The minigames (rover/truck race, ice drilling and collection, water purification, greenhouse, shielding maze, spacecraft quarters), code-generated pixel art icons, and the rocket launch animation.
  • Web Audio API: Real-time synthesized music and sound effects with no external audio files, including the race soundtrack and the solar panel punk rock track.
  • Web Speech API (speech synthesis): Voice narration for Commander Lampião's lines in Brazilian Portuguese and English.
  • MutationObserver: On-screen PT→EN translation system.
  • Intl.DisplayNames: Country names localized into the selected language.
  • Google Fonts: Roboto (readability) and Press Start 2P (title screen).

WHAT IS THE CREATIVE ELEMENT OF YOUR PROJECT? 

→ In an integrated way, Under Space incorporates data from NASA programs directly into its gameplay—from the story context to the design of its challenges—all set within a playful and nostalgic environment. The game follows a challenging approach that makes learning about NASA programs, resources, and resource management feel lighthearted, creating an engaging and thought-provoking experience for the player. 

WHAT FACTORS DID YOUR TEAM TAKE INTO CONSIDERATION? 

→ The team considered factors such as facilitating education through a nostalgic visual identity, simplifying and integrating data organically, and creating a lightweight, intuitive interface.
